issues.failure_explanation: b_m is defined only for arguments in {0,...,2^m-1}. At k=2^ell-1 the third identity reads b_{ell+1}(2^{ell+1}) = 0 b_ell(2^ell), and both b_{ell+1}(2^{ell+1}) and b_ell(2^ell) are undefined (2^{ell+1} has no length-(ell+1) binary expansion, so the proof step 'follows analogously' also fails there). The quantifier k in {0,...,2^ell-1} therefore includes a point at which the stated identity is not even formed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the third identity to 0 <= k <= 2^ell-2, or delete it (it is never used).
issues.overall_effect: Only the lemma's third identity at the endpoint is affected; Corollary cor:dyadic-refinement uses just the first two identities (arguments 2k, 2k+1 <= 2^{ell+1}-1), so nothing downstream is invalidated.
issues.title: Third binary-shift identity is ill-defined at the boundary k=2^ell-1
issues.why_classification: A forced, one-line quantifier/domain repair of a boundary instance with zero downstream effect and no change to any claim that is used.

issues.failure_explanation: When p_w = 0 the convention prescribes cos^2 theta_w := 0 and sin^2 theta_w := 0, which no angle theta_w in [0,pi/2] (indeed no real angle) satisfies; so the angle map is undefined exactly on the zero-mass nodes where this branch applies, even though the circuit construction applies an actual rotation R(theta_w) for every node. The proof of Proposition prop:trig_factorization silently uses the different, coherent convention theta_w := 0 (i.e. cos^2 theta_w = 1), directly contradicting the stated convention.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Declare theta_w := 0 (any fixed angle works) when p_w = 0, aligning the definition with its use in the proof and circuit.
issues.overall_effect: No downstream mathematical damage: zero-mass nodes have only zero-mass descendants, so all affected amplitudes vanish for any chosen angle, and Proposition prop:trig_factorization, Lemma lem:inductive_state and Theorem theorem:Grover-Rudolph survive verbatim. As written, however, the angle assignment is ill-defined and internally inconsistent.
issues.title: Zero-mass branch of the angle convention defines no angle and conflicts with the proof's convention
issues.why_classification: A forced one-line definitional repair that is already operative in the paper's own proof; every substantive claim and guarantee is preserved verbatim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the first $(j-1)$ bits of an integer corresponds to extracting its suffix.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:suffix-extraction with shift s yields the suffix z_{s+1}...z_n of length n-s. Instantiated with s = j-1 as written, the left side equals z_j...z_n (length n-j+1), not z_{n-j+2}...z_n (length j-1); the two agree only when n-j+1 = j-1. Counterexample: n=3, j=2, any k with z_2=1 gives LHS b_2(floor(k/2)) = z_2 z_3, while the claimed RHS is z_3. The correct invocation is s = n-j+1: b_{j-1}(floor(2^{-(n-j+1)} k)) = z_{n-j+2}...z_n. The accompanying prose 'truncating the first (j-1) bits' is wrong for the same reason.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shift by s = n-j+1 (and the length by b_{j-1}) in the display and in the prose phrase.
issues.overall_effect: A false justification step inside the proof. The identification it justifies (the last j-1 qubits hold bits z_{n-j+2}...z_n) is correct by the register conventions and is what the induction actually uses, so the lemma's statement and its inductive argument are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong shift in the suffix-extraction display inside the proof of Lemma lem:inductive_state
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced directly by Lemma lem:suffix-extraction; the justified identification and the induction are correct, so no inference or claim changes.

issues.failure_explanation: From the example's own (correct) table and definitions, gamma(0),...,gamma(7) = (0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4), so d_1 = gamma(1) xor gamma(0) = 1, d_4 = 6 xor 2 = 4, etc.: the correct sequences are (d_1,...,d_7) = (1,2,1,4,1,2,1) and (j(1),...,j(7)) = (1,2,1,3,1,2,1). The stated sequences are wrong at k = 1,3,4,5,7 (they are the bit-reversed values, i.e. positions counted from the wrong end): e.g. g_0=000 -> g_1=100 flips the first letter, giving d_1=1, j(1)=1, not d_1=4, j(1)=3; and g_3=010 -> g_4=011 flips the third letter, giving d_4=4, j(4)=3, not d_4=1, j(4)=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the two sequences from the stated definitions: (d_k) = (1,2,1,4,1,2,1), (j(k)) = (1,2,1,3,1,2,1).
issues.overall_effect: Confined to the illustrative example: the Gray words themselves are listed correctly, and no other result or construction uses these (d_k), (j(k)) values.
issues.title: Example's flip-mask and flip-index sequences contradict its own Gray-code definitions and table
issues.why_classification: A local computational error with a forced correction; nothing else in the paper depends on these values, so all claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: so the net trailing toggle is $X^{S_{2^m-1}(\mathbf u)}=\rI$ and no residual Pauli factor remains.
(for $m=1$ the ladder reduces to the standard two-gate controlled-$\RY$ synthesis and the same conclusion holds)
In particular, the circuit uses exactly $2^{m}$ single-qubit $\RY$ gates and $2^{m}-1$ $\CNOT$ gates and requires no ancillas.

issues.failure_explanation: In the m-bit binary-reflected Gray code, flip position r occurs exactly 2^{m-r} times among j(1),...,j(2^m-1) (the ruler function; for m=3 the paper's own Gray list gives flip positions (1,2,1,3,1,2,1)), not 2^{m-1} times. Hence the trailing parity is S_{2^m-1}(u) = sum_r u_r 2^{m-r} == u_m (mod 2), so on every control branch whose last letter u_m = 1 the ladder applies an odd number of X toggles to the target q_1 and acts as RY(phi_u) X (equivalently X RY(phi_u)) instead of the pure rotation RY(phi_u). Direct check for m=2, branch u=(0,1): the ladder gives RY(alpha_{00}+alpha_{10}-alpha_{11}-alpha_{01}) X = RY(phi_{01}) X, not RY(phi_{01}). Thus the decomposition eq:ucr_ladder is false for every m >= 1: with the stated Walsh-Hadamard angles the ladder equals UCRY(phi) composed with one additional CNOT(q_{1+m} -> q_1). The claims that each control index appears 2^{m-1} times, that no residual Pauli factor remains, and that m=1 'reduces to the standard two-gate controlled-RY synthesis' are all false (with a single CNOT, branch u=1 yields RY(alpha_1-alpha_0) X, which no angle choice makes a pure rotation; the standard controlled-RY synthesis uses two CNOTs). The intermediate identities 'sign (-1)^{S_{k-1}}' and 'S_{k-1}(u) = <u,g_k>' are also each off by one index (the correct relations are (-1)^{S_k} and S_k(u) = <u,g_k>); these two slips cancel, so the angle part of the conclusion is correct and only the residual toggle is wrong.

failure_location.quote: Finally, along the Gray-code ladder each control index $r\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ appears exactly $2^{m-1}$ times

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Close the Gray cycle: insert one additional CNOT with control q_{1+m}=q_j (the bit that flips between g_{2^m-1} and g_0) and target q_1 at the beginning or end of the ladder. Then the flip counts are 2^{m-r} for r<m and 2 for r=m, all even, the residual toggle vanishes for every m >= 1 (for m=1 this is precisely the standard two-CNOT controlled-RY synthesis), and the Walsh-Hadamard angle transform is unchanged. Update the CNOT count to 2^m (and 2^{j-1} per stage in the conclusion paragraph), Algorithm alg:ucry_gray_ladder, and Figure fig:graycode_ladder_generic, and replace the false parity argument with the correct ruler-function count.
issues.overall_effect: The ancilla-free transpilation asserted for every Grover-Rudolph stage j in {2,...,n} is incorrect as stated: Algorithm alg:ucry_gray_ladder outputs a circuit equal to UCRY only up to an extra CNOT on branches with last control bit 1; the per-stage counts '2^{j-1} RY gates and 2^{j-1}-1 CNOT gates' in the conclusion paragraph are wrong; Figure fig:graycode_ladder_generic lacks the closing CNOT; and the abstract/introduction claims of an explicit ancilla-free transpilation with full correctness proofs are unsupported as written. Theorem theorem:Grover-Rudolph and its proof do not depend on this section and are unaffected.
issues.title: Gray-code ladder misses the closing CNOT: residual X on all branches with last control bit 1
issues.why_classification: Not a degenerate case: the stated equality fails for every m >= 1, the proof's pivotal combinatorial parity claim is false and must be replaced, the construction (one more gate), the advertised CNOT count, the algorithm, and the figure must all change. But the repair is contained and standard and preserves the advertised result -- an ancilla-free Gray-code ladder transpilation with the same Walsh-Hadamard angles and linear gate counts -- so there is no major loss and no new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: consistent with finite-shot sampling fluctuations and with the finite-precision
Possible directions for future work include: (i) sharper a priori stability bounds that link angle quantization

issues.failure_explanation: The Conclusions assert that the paper 'discussed ... how finite-precision approximations of rotation angles affect the output distribution and how such errors propagate through successive Grover--Rudolph stages.' The source contains no such discussion or analysis: the numerics section only simulates one 3-qubit example and remarks in a single sentence that the observed discrepancies are consistent with finite-shot fluctuations and finite-precision angle representation, and stability bounds linking angle quantization to output error are explicitly listed as future work. The claimed coverage is unsupported by the paper's content.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the clause or weaken it to match the single finite-precision remark actually made (or add the missing propagation analysis).
issues.overall_effect: Only the Conclusions coverage sentence is affected; no formal result changes, but readers are told an error-propagation discussion exists in the paper when it does not.
issues.title: Conclusions claim a discussion of angle-precision error propagation that the paper does not contain
issues.why_classification: Removing or softening one unsupported sentence repairs the issue with no mathematical loss and no effect on any result.
